proposal: The Mandate recommends reassessing all US aid programs in Latin America and ending those that have not produced results. USAID would then focus on free-market fundamentals (property rights, a functioning judiciary, labor and pension reform, lower taxes, deregulation), challenge socialist ideas, fund private-sector partnerships and pro-market civil society, and commit to shifting the whole regional portfolio to local organizations by 2030. It notes that the first-term America Crece investment initiative was cancelled.
remaining: A published results-based review of remaining Latin America programs.
Funding for pro-market civil society, university centers and think tanks as the text describes.
A commitment to move the regional portfolio to local organizations by 2030.
A successor to America Crece or another investment-promotion program.

status_summary: In the successor structure the reassess-and-terminate element happened through the global review rather than a results-based regional one: the Secretary of State announced on 2025-03-10 that about 5,200 of 6,200 USAID programs (about 83 percent) were eliminated, WOLA, an advocacy group, estimated from a March 2025 memo to Congress that more than 84 percent of USAID assistance to Latin America and the Caribbean was cut, and USAID's remaining operations merged into State on 2025-07-01. For the positive agenda, State's five-year strategy, as reported by Devex on 2026-01-29, gives the Western Hemisphere and East Asia about 40 percent of foreign assistance, shifts from grant aid toward trade and private-sector growth and selects partners partly by security, migration and voting alignment, and the National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 calls for commercial diplomacy and for tying aid terms to winding down adversary influence. Against the text, WOLA reports that State's democracy bureau cancelled 389 of 391 democracy grants, which runs against support for pro-market and democratic civil society, and no 2030 localization commitment, free-market reform program or America Crece successor was found. The stage is in_progress at the low end because the terminations are operative and the regional reorientation is stated in strategy, while the text's positive program elements are not shown.

timeline.event: The Secretary of State announced that the review of USAID programs was complete, with about 5,200 of 6,200 programs (about 83 percent) eliminated worldwide and the rest to be managed under State.
USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department.

The White House released the National Security Strategy (cover dated November 2025), whose Western Hemisphere section calls for commercial diplomacy, DFC and other financing for US investment, and aid terms contingent on winding down adversary influence.

WOLA reported its estimate, based on a March 2025 memo to Congress, that more than 84 percent of USAID aid to Latin America and the Caribbean was eliminated, and, citing a Senate source, that State's democracy bureau cancelled 389 of 391 democracy grants; it also noted a 20 billion dollar financial rescue for Argentina (outside aid appropriations).

Devex reported that State's five-year strategy would give the Western Hemisphere and East Asia together about 40 percent of foreign assistance, shift from grant aid toward trade and private-sector growth, and select partners by security ties, migration cooperation and voting alignment; the strategy gives no dollar amounts.

title: Reassess Latin America aid, end failed programs, back free markets and localize by 2030
uncertainties: The 84 percent figure for Latin America is WOLA's estimate from a memo to Congress that was not read; the 83 percent figure is global and is computed from the program counts in the AP report, whose page shows no date (the announcement was on a Monday about six weeks after 2025-01-20, consistent with 2025-03-10). The State five-year strategy was read only through a Devex newsletter copy hosted by the USAID Alumni Association, not the State document; the article does not name the strategy. The National Security Strategy was read directly; its cover reads November 2025 and its release date of 2025-12-04 comes from Lawfare (the earlier placeholder date of the first of November was replaced). Its Western Hemisphere section does not address local organizations and mentions property rights only through opposition to expropriation. No revival of America Crece, no 2030 localization commitment and no funding line for pro-market civil society were found. Executive Order 14217 (signed 2025-02-19, published 2025-02-25) lists the Inter-American Foundation for reduction to its statutory functions; the foundation is a separate agency not named in the Mandate text and the order is background only; litigation over it was not verified. The Argentina rescue is Treasury financial support, not foreign aid. Assistance to Haiti and Venezuelan migrants was not examined. WOLA also notes that FY2026 democracy funds were appropriated but their use was uncertain as of January 2026.
